evidence.claim: The paved route crosses salt marsh and creeks, passing maritime forest, farm fields and historic churches.
evidence.quote: The route traverses salt marsh, creeks, maritime forests, farm fields and historic churches from the Intracoastal Waterway to the Atlantic Ocean.

evidence.claim: The paved route

evidence.claim: Live oaks arch over the island’s main road.

evidence.claim: The Federal Highway Administration’s National Scenic Byway description highlights this landscape alongside roadside sweetgrass baskets and local produce.

evidence.claim: SC 174 serves as the island’s main spine, with smaller roads and lanes branching toward more distant parts of the island.
evidence.quote: serves as the primary spine road for the island, with smaller country roads and lanes intersecting it and leading to more distant areas of the island.

evidence.claim: The Dawhoo crossing has changed three times: a manually operated, single-lane swing bridge opened in 1920, followed by an electrically powered two-lane span in 1950.
evidence.quote: The first bridge opened in 1920 and was a single-lane swing span that was opened manually by the bridge tender.

evidence.claim: an electrically powered two-lane span in 1950.
evidence.quote: The second bridge opened in 1950. It was a two-lane electrically powered swing span.

evidence.claim: The present bridge, dedicated in 1993, replaced a swing span whose openings for boats delayed road traffic.
evidence.quote: This is the third bridge in the same location, replacing a swing bridge that caused traffic delays when it opened for boats.

evidence.claim: dedicated in 1993
evidence.quote: The current bridge was dedicated on September 25, 1993.

evidence.claim: It honors legislator McKinley Washington Jr., who led the effort to fund the replacement.
evidence.quote: The bridge is named for McKinley Washington Jr., who served in the South Carolina General Assembly, representing the area and leading the effort to appropriate funds to replace the bridge.

evidence.claim: The road itself changed too: straightening and paving about 1940 left an older section isolated as Wescott Road, an oak-lined dirt road established in the Colonial era.
evidence.quote: The road was established in the Colonial era.  This section was isolated when S.C. Highway 174 was straightened and paved about 1940.

evidence.claim: an oak-lined dirt road
evidence.quote: is an oak-lined dirt road

evidence.claim: From the bridge, follow the island road past homes, prayer chapels, churches and country stores.
evidence.quote: past small homes, prayer chapels, churches, and country stores

evidence.claim: The journey ends at Edisto Beach, bordered to the north and east by Edisto Beach State Park.
evidence.quote: Edisto Beach State Park borders the town to the north and east.

evidence.claim: Near the coast, the park’s trails continue through maritime forest to a shell midden and an old survey monument.
evidence.quote: The trails wind through Edisto Island's maritime forest, leading to sites such as a Native American shell midden dated to 2000 BC, and a survey monument placed by Alexander Bache in 1850.

evidence.claim: The congregation’s history reaches back further than the building: it was founded in 1685, while the present church dates to 1831.
evidence.quote: The congregation was founded in 1685 and the current church building was constructed in 1831.

evidence.claim: A burying ground adjoins the church.
evidence.quote: The church's burying ground is adjacent to the building.

evidence.claim: The building entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1971, and the congregation belongs to the Presbyterian Church (USA).
evidence.quote: The church was added to the National Register of Historic Places on June 24, 1971. The congregation is a member of the Presbyterian Church (USA).

evidence.claim: The burying ground sits beside the church building.
evidence.quote: The church's burying ground is adjacent to the building.

evidence.claim: Three Bleak Hall outbuildings survive at Botany Bay, including an icehouse with pointed windows and wooden spires.
evidence.quote: Three outbuildings from the Bleak Hall Plantation, thought to date from the 1840s, remain on the Botany Bay preserve.

evidence.claim: an icehouse with pointed windows and wooden spires.
evidence.quote: One of these buildings is a 1 1/2-story icehouse

evidence.claim: pointed windows and wooden spires.
evidence.quote: each with two pointed windows and a small balcony.  Three-level wooden spires

evidence.claim: Plantation owner John Townsend sold Sea Island cotton to lace-makers in Belgium and France; the 1860 census recorded him as holding 272 people enslaved.
evidence.quote: his cotton commanded a high price from lace-makers in Belgium and France

evidence.claim: the 1860 census recorded him as holding 272 people enslaved.
evidence.quote: In the census of 1860, John Townsend was registered as the owner of 272 enslaved laborers.

evidence.claim: Bleak Hall and Sea Cloud were combined as Botany Bay Plantation in 1933.
evidence.quote: The Bleak Hall and Sea Cloud plantations remained in the Townsend family until 1933, when they were bought by Dr. James C. Greenway, part of the Lauder Greenway Family, who combined them to form Botany Bay Plantation.

evidence.claim: The property was bequeathed to South Carolina as a wildlife preserve in 1977, but opened to the public in 2008 after the owner’s widow died.
evidence.quote: John Meyer died in 1977; his widow remarried as Margaret Pepper, and remained on the plantation, continuing to manage and improve the property for conservation purposes, until her death in 2007.

evidence.claim: Bleak Hall’s main house burned during or shortly after the Civil War and was replaced with a house combining Victorian styles.
evidence.quote: This house burned down during or shortly after the war, and a new one was built in a mix of Victorian styles.

evidence.claim: Trails through Edisto Beach State Park’s maritime forest reach a Native American shell midden and an 1850 survey monument placed by Alexander Bache.
evidence.quote: The trails wind through Edisto Island's maritime forest, leading to sites such as a Native American shell midden dated to 2000 BC, and a survey monument placed by Alexander Bache in 1850.

evidence.claim: The park itself developed on land the Edisto Company donated in 1935.
evidence.quote: It was created on land donated in 1935 by the Edisto Company.

evidence.claim: The Civilian Conservation Corps built the park, and many of its original buildings remain in use.
evidence.quote: The park was one of the first South Carolina state parks, developed by the Civilian Conservation Corps.

evidence.claim: many of its original buildings remain in use.
evidence.quote: Many of the original buildings built by the CCC still stand and are in use currently.

evidence.claim: At the Edisto Interpretive Center, interactive displays explain the ACE Basin estuarine reserve.
evidence.quote: The center includes an exhibit teaching visitors about the ACE Basin estuarine reserve through interactive displays.
